subject: Media Literacy
title: Encrypted Messaging
description: A quick win: understand Encrypted Messaging.

hook.text: A journalist's source was exposed through unencrypted messages. Encryption makes messages unreadable to anyone but the recipient.

buildup.text: End-to-end encryption ensures only the sender and receiver can read messages — not the platform, not the government.

discovery.text: Signal, WhatsApp, and iMessage offer end-to-end encryption. Regular SMS and many other apps do not.

twist.text: Encryption protects content but not metadata. Who you message, when, and how often is still visible.

climax.text: Encrypted messaging is the minimum standard for private digital communication. Anything less is a postcard.

punchline.text: An unencrypted message is a postcard. Everyone between you and the recipient can read it.

quiz.question: What does end-to-end encryption not protect?
options: Metadata — who you message, when, and how often
